授業概要
市民は、ある出来事を記憶し、別の出来事を忘れるよう教育されます。過去の記憶は、現在の理解や未来の構想と相互に関わり合っています。本授業では、「記憶」、より正確には「想起（remembering）」に焦点を当て、これを社会政治的および倫理・批判的な視点から考察します。まず、過去がどのように記憶されるのか（Wertsch, 2004）を検討し、そのうえで、過去はいかに記憶されるべきか（Campbell, 2014）という規範的な問いへと議論を発展させます。こうした記憶をめぐる考察は、時間、身体、アイデンティティ、関係性、連帯といったシティズンシップに関わる諸テーマを構成するとともに、それらへの理解を深めることにもつながります。
Citizens are educated to remember some and forget others. Memory of the past interacts with understanding of the present and with envisioning the future. This course zooms in on memory, or more precisely, remembering from sociopolitical and ethico-critical perspectives. It discusses how the past is remembered (Wertsch, 2004) before venturing further to explore how the past should be remembered (Campbell, 2014). The discussion of memory is constitutive of, and contributes to, citizenship-related themes such as time, body, identity, relationality, and solidarity.

全体の教育目標
The course reads and discusses the chapters in Wertsch (2004) and Campbell (2014). Through the course, students will gain critical perspectives to understand contemporary sociopolitical life and relations through the lens of memory/remembering.
個別の教育目標
After completing the course, students should be able to consider the sociopolitical role of memory in their individual research.
授業計画
We will read and discuss one or two chapters each week.
キーワード
memory; remembering; time; body; citizenship
授業の進め方
Each class starts with one student summarising the reading assignment. We will clarify the text before addressing student comments and questions, which should be prepared by all students for each class. Although the text is in English, students are encouraged to participate in class discussions using either English or Japanese.
テキスト
Wertsch, James V. (2004). Voices of Collective Remembering. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
Campbell, Sue (2014). Our Faithfulness to the Past: The Ethics And Politics Of Memory (C. M. Koggel & R. Jacobsen Eds.). Oxford: Oxford University Press.
Copies will be provided in class.
